title: Research and evidence team
description: Research a bounded question, verify material claims, and assess relevant architecture, design, security, or performance implications.
intent: Answer the requested question using project constraints and cited sources. Separate gathering, independent evidence checks, and relevant domain interpretation. This is research/review scope; do not implement changes, contact vendors, or publish by default.

assignments.task: Frame decision criteria, gather supporting and contradictory sources, normalize comparisons, and return conclusions with citations, versions/dates, assumptions, and unknowns.
Independently inspect the completed source packet: citation support, freshness, comparable conditions, calculations, inference boundaries, and remaining uncertainty.
Assess feasibility, integration, contracts, ownership, and consequential structural trade-offs using the completed research.
assignments.when: The question affects architecture or technology selection.

assignments.task: Assess user/product fit, interaction implications, design-system compatibility, and accessibility requirements without inventing user research.
assignments.when: The question affects product flows, UI, design systems, or user needs.

assignments.task: Assess security/privacy implications and constraints without treating vendor claims as established controls.
assignments.when: The researched decision affects trust boundaries, sensitive data, authorization, or security controls.

assignments.task: Assess benchmark comparability, resource costs, budgets, and measurement gaps without claiming source research proves project performance.
assignments.when: The researched decision depends on performance, scale, resource cost, or benchmark claims.

completion: The bounded question is answered against explicit project criteria with direct citations supporting material claims.
Evidence validation follows completed research; applicable domain assessments return results or explicit gaps.
Facts, vendor assertions, observations, inference, recommendations, and unknowns are distinguished.
Conflicting evidence is reconciled or retained as uncertainty; practical next validations are stated without unrequested implementation.
